proposed_from.topic: Correct the marginal-to-conditional quasi-stayer gap in de Chaisemartin, D'Haultfœuille and Vazquez-Bare's continuous-treatment DiD Theorem 1. For iid two-period data with static potential outcomes, conditional parallel trends, known compact treatment support, a baseline trend m bounded by M and L-Lipschitz, and conditional mean causal movement bounded by K|delta|, define g(d,delta)=E[Delta Y|D1=d,Delta D=delta], nu_P(B)=E[sgn(Delta D)1{D1 in B}], and C_P={u: |u|<=M, Lip(u)<=L, |g(d,delta)-u(d)|<=K|delta| on the observed support}. Prove that the full-observed-law sharp WAOSS set is exactly Theta(P)={(E[sgn(Delta D)Delta Y]-integral u dnu_P)/E|Delta D|:u in C_P}; every u must be attained by a legal full potential-outcome law matching P. Prove compact attained interval geometry, the exact point-identification criterion R(P)=max_C integral u dnu_P-min_C integral u dnu_P=0, recovery of the published formula under conditional zero-support, observable obstacle-envelope compatibility, constant-one clipping stability, certified finite LP approximations, and a uniformly honest outer confidence interval on the fixed beta-Hölder, bounded-density, bounded-outcome finite-rectangle support subclass. Do not claim novelty for common-zero-baseline scalar bounded-slope intervals, already in arXiv:2405.04465v4, or invalidate the source's separate parametric estimate. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Derived the exact affine lift b=(g(D1,Delta D)-u(D1))/Delta D, Y1^u(t)=Y1, Y2^u(t)=Y2+b(t-D2), which preserves the entire observed law, realizes trend u, and has |b|<=K. Derived obstacle clipping with exact constant-one Hausdorff error and checked finite Theta=[-3/5,1] and continuous-density Theta=[-4/7,4/7] witnesses; signed cancellation, equality constraints, empty classes, support versions, denominator boundaries, and the common-baseline prior-art collision were checked. The lift also explains why marginal quasi-stayers alone cannot identify a baseline-specific trend: observed increments constrain u only through support-local cones, while the signed baseline measure transmits unresolved components directly into WAOSS endpoints. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Complete the uniform band-to-finite-program lemma on every allowed rectangle union, including boundary-aware regression coverage, signed-DKW control, measurable endpoint construction, and the stated ratio error. EARLY KILL TEST: Prove that lemma first on a fixed rectangle union with touching boundaries and one component separated from zero changes; if it needs extra density smoothness, strict feasibility, or stronger support assumptions than K4, pivot. seed_details.title: Full-observed-law completion frontier for WAOSS
seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction, Assumption 4, Theorem 1, its proof in the arXiv source, and the closing discussion of the parametric approach were inspected.
seed_details.opportunity: Replace the unsupported passage from marginal quasi-stayers to the baseline-conditional value \(g(d,0)\) by a sharp set over support-compatible baseline trends and an observed-law-preserving potential-outcome construction.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: After conditioning on \(D_1=d\), do not evaluate \(g(d,0)\) unless zero belongs to the corresponding conditional support; retain the support-local cone instead.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for the source title with correction or erratum, conditional quasi-stayers, and WAOSS partial identification returned no theorem for the varying-baseline signed frontier.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from the source decomposition because one merely replaces a missing limit by an interval.
seed_details.rebuttal: The nontrivial step is constructive full-law sharpness: every feasible trend must be pasted into static potential outcomes while preserving the entire observed joint distribution.
seed_details.burned_reason: All eight proposal seeds were exhausted, merged, or ruled out without an in-scope lift to the field floor.

seed_details.title: Observable compatibility and exact target-identification criterion
seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction, the identified-set diameter construction, the principal consistency theorem, and the conclusion were inspected in the published manuscript.
seed_details.opportunity: Characterize feasibility by two observable obstacle envelopes and distinguish identification of the signed WAOSS functional from identification of the entire baseline trend through \(R(P)=0\).
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace injectivity of the nuisance map by zero diameter of its image under the signed baseline functional.
seed_details.destination_search: The exact target--method search for obstacle envelopes and signed WAOSS diameter found completeness diagnostics for other inverse problems but no continuous-treatment DiD result.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from convex analysis because a scalar image is a singleton exactly when its maximum and minimum agree.
seed_details.rebuttal: The scalar identity is elementary, but the observable envelope equivalence, empty-model certificate, and cancellation examples require the support-local causal completion theorem.
seed_details.burned_reason: All eight proposal seeds were exhausted, merged, or ruled out without an in-scope lift to the field floor.

seed_details.title: Transport dual for the signed bounded-Lipschitz frontier
seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction, the weighted-functional restriction, the convex-program characterization, and the conclusion were inspected.
seed_details.opportunity: Derive a measure-valued transport dual for the signed WAOSS support function, making cross-baseline cancellation and the cost of Lipschitz coupling explicit.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace a positive policy weight by the Jordan decomposition of the signed baseline measure and dualize the two-sided obstacles jointly with Lipschitz transport.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for signed-measure Lipschitz obstacle duals locate general optimal-transport duality but no causal WAOSS formulation or full-law completion result.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Kantorovich duality after writing the Lipschitz constraint.
seed_details.rebuttal: A generic dual is not the causal result; its value depends on first deriving the exact observable obstacles and signed measure from legal full-law completions.
seed_details.burned_reason: All eight proposal seeds were exhausted, merged, or ruled out without an in-scope lift to the field floor.

seed_details.title: Certified finite programs for continuous support
seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction, Proposition 2 and its convex-combination proof, the finite linear programs in equation (6), the endpoint limit theory, and Section 7 were inspected.
seed_details.opportunity: Convert infinitely many support-local cones and a global Lipschitz restriction into attained finite inner and outer programs with an exact constant-one clipping certificate.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the paper's finite-support vector by obstacle envelopes on a compact support, then prove that mesh feasibility extends and clips back to the continuum class.
seed_details.destination_search: The closest 2025 LP-value work begins with a finite program; no result found supplies the required continuum-to-finite causal certificate on rectangle unions.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate by gridding a Lipschitz function and invoking finite LP convergence.
seed_details.rebuttal: Naive gridding gives no inner lift at touching boundaries and no uniform endpoint guarantee under equality constraints; the exact clipping retraction supplies both without Slater conditions.
seed_details.burned_reason: All eight proposal seeds were exhausted, merged, or ruled out without an in-scope lift to the field floor.

seed_details.title: Uniformly honest outer inference for optimized WAOSS endpoints
seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction, the calibrated relaxation defining projection endpoints, the uniform coverage theorem, the computational algorithm, and the conclusion were inspected.
seed_details.opportunity: Combine a boundary-aware band for \(g\), signed empirical-process control, deterministic mesh error, and denominator error into one measurable finite-program outer interval.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Before calibrating endpoint optimization, replace finitely indexed moments by a simultaneous band over the observed rectangle support and certify its finite relaxation.
seed_details.destination_search: Calibrated projection treats finite-dimensional moment systems; uniform regression-band papers do not propagate their bands through this support-dependent signed endpoint program.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate by feeding a uniform confidence band into a relaxed optimization problem.
seed_details.rebuttal: Uniform inclusion is delicate at support boundaries, touching rectangles, nonunique optimizers, and random signed objectives; the band-to-program lemma is the unresolved theorem-level step.
seed_details.burned_reason: All eight proposal seeds were exhausted, merged, or ruled out without an in-scope lift to the field floor.

seed_details.title: Minimax inference across the quasi-stayer point-to-set transition
seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction, the slow-mover bias-correction construction, the distributional theorem, the uniformity discussion, and the conclusion were inspected.
seed_details.opportunity: Derive the minimax confidence-length frontier as conditional quasi-stayer mass vanishes and support holes open.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Allow the identifying boundary point to leave conditional support, so the local experiment changes from irregular point identification to set identification.
seed_details.destination_search: Slow-mover theory retains point identification, while honest convex-class inference fixes the identified object; no joint topology-changing frontier was found.
seed_details.red_team: This is a routine combination of slow-mover trimming and partial-identification confidence intervals.
seed_details.rebuttal: The local experiment and loss change discontinuously when the target becomes set-valued, so neither existing limit theory transfers directly.
seed_details.burned_reason: All eight proposal seeds were exhausted, merged, or ruled out without an in-scope lift to the field floor.

seed_details.title: Boundary-adaptive regression coverage on finite rectangle unions
seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction, the boundary-adaptive local-polynomial construction, the uniform Gaussian approximation, the confidence-band result, and the conclusion were inspected.
seed_details.opportunity: Construct a component-respecting conditional-mean band that remains uniform at outer and touching boundaries and feeds a finite WAOSS program.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Adapt boundary-local polynomial coverage from a conditional-density process to the outcome regression on a known union of support rectangles, without averaging across disconnected components.
seed_details.destination_search: The destination search found boundary-adaptive density bands and generic series bands, but not the required conditional-mean band coupled to signed partial-identification optimization.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from existing boundary-adaptive local-polynomial confidence bands.
seed_details.rebuttal: As a standalone result the objection largely holds; its only credible role is as a lemma inside the full inference seed.

seed_details.title: Reduction to the common-zero-baseline bounded-slope interval
seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction, the no-quasi-stayer bounded-effect section, its sharp intersection-bound theorem and proof, and the conclusion were inspected in version 4.
seed_details.opportunity: Use the common-zero-baseline design as an exact reduction test for the varying-baseline completion frontier.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Permit heterogeneous baseline doses and both signs of treatment change, forcing global cross-baseline Lipschitz coupling rather than one scalar baseline trend.
seed_details.destination_search: Later versions and related continuous-treatment DiD papers preserve the common-baseline geometry; none found supplies the varying-baseline signed set.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from the published common-zero-baseline scalar bounded-slope interval.
seed_details.rebuttal: The scalar case is indeed occupied and receives no novelty credit; it is retained only as a mandatory reduction, not as the kernel.
